extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology containing metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar. The corpus spans seven decades, containing 73K papers and 210K figures for open scientific research in computational linguistics.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The corpus was constructed by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. Full-text extraction was performed using GROBID, figures were extracted using PDFFigures, and the corpus was linked to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) using its Graph API. The dataset undergoes annual updates by monitoring URL changes to identify new additions to the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, containing 73,285 conference journal and workshop papers in the computational linguistics domain published from 1952 to September 2022. PDF files longer than 50 pages (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks) were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual quality checking of 21 documents to assess full text quality across three aspects: metadata, general texts, and contents in specialized formats. For topic classification, a pre-trained language model was trained on 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels, then used to predict silver-labeled topic information for the full corpus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Manual quality assessment of 21 documents for full-text extraction quality across metadata, general texts, and specialized format contents
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID for full-text extraction from PDFs, PDFFigures for figure and table extraction, language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010) for language detection, pre-trained language model for topic classification
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers, not comprehensive like S2ORC. Full-text extraction fails mostly for papers between 2000-2015. The corpus is unlabeled, lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels. Only open-source PDF2text toolkits are used due to budget constraints, though paid services might yield higher-quality full texts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain, including temporal topic trends analysis, observing trends in computational linguistics, and enabling various research tasks through structured full texts, enriched metadata, and figures.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available from HuggingFace. Future plans include updating OCL by year to keep it current with ACL Anthology data, with the ultimate solution being to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology itself.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Papers longer than 50 pages were removed, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks. Language detection was performed using a public toolkit with title and abstract as inputs. Research topics were automatically detected and added to enable further analysis.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Full-text extraction from PDF files using GROBID toolkit. Data structured according to S2ORC-JSON format including metadata, authors, body text with citations, references, and sections. Dataset provided in both CSV and Apache Parquet formats. Metadata obtained from ACL Anthology website for accuracy.

name.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.

description.evidence: Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar). The ACL OCL spans seven decades, containing 73K papers, alongside 210K figures.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC (Lo et al., 2020), since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology... We observe that our full-text extraction fail mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015... The OCL corpus is an unlabeled resource, lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels... Due to constraints on budget, only open-source toolkits are considered, although it is acknowledged that some paid PDF2text services might yield higher-quality full texts.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain... We spotlight how ACL OCL applies to observe trends in computational linguistics... The structured full texts, enriched metadata from Semantic Scholar Academic Graph, and figures provided by OCL can benefit existing research tasks as well as enable more opportunities.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Our dataset is available from HuggingFace... In the future, we will work on the data currency of OCL, which aims to keep OCL up-to-date with the ACL Anthology data. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive. The ultimate solution is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, thus hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks. We add automatically detected fields such as language and topic to enable further analysis. To detect the language in which a document is written, we utilize a public language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010) with its title and abstract as inputs.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files... We take the S2ORC-JSON format used by Lo et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2020) for our full-text schema, which includes complete information parsed from PDF files, such as metadata, authors, and body text with citations, references, sections and etc... Meta information is included, as the website's version is more accurate than that obtained by PDF extraction
